//: ywr-harness declaration. Repo-specific values live HERE so the plugin's scripts stay identical in every repo (ADR 0010). Placed once by /harness-init and never overwritten — edit it freely. Every command-shaped field is a SELECTOR from a closed set defined in the plugin, never a command string: this file is in the working tree, and the scripts print commands that get run (ADR 0012). A gate that is this repo's own script is declared as a script gate — closed-set runner + validated repo-relative path, still never a command string (ADR 0024).

docs.//site_title: The <title>/header of the generated docs surfaces (docs.html · docs.artifact.html; the customer surface derives its default from it). THIS declaration is the source — the DOCS_SITE_TITLE env var is a one-off override only, so a harness-init re-run or CI rebuild can never revert a committed title (ADR 0050). Convention: '<repo> · <purpose>', same as artifact titles (ADR 0032). Empty = the builder's default. Display text only — it is escaped into HTML and never reaches a command.

//handoff: Resume-point doc the slice close updates (reporting only — never reaches a command). A single file serves a single active work line; a value ending in '/' declares a DIRECTORY holding one resume file per work line (multi-writer repos), each named after the work line, never after a person (ADR 0040). Either form, the handoff is a resume point, not a ledger: the close that supersedes a Current state section moves it to docs/handoff-archive/<same filename>.
//artifacts: Declared claude.ai Artifacts (ADR 0032). When this repo publishes an Artifact (onboarding guide, docs page from docs/docs.artifact.html, …), declare it here: the gate emitter checks that 'readme' carries each declared url and each declared title starts with the repo name (naming convention: <repo> · <purpose>), and CI fails on a violation. The gate cannot see claude.ai, so an undeclared Artifact is invisible to it — the emitter reports the check as disabled until something is declared.

review.//: Regexes. They select and report — they cannot name an executable, so free strings are safe here.
review.//docs_only: Surfaces that carry no executable meaning. When EVERY changed file matches, the review tier is 'skip' and deterministic gates suffice.
review.//harness_layer: Code-bearing surfaces that are tooling rather than product. When every code-bearing file is confined here, the tier is 'small'.
review.//critical: Surfaces where a weaker review is worst. ANY match forces tier 'full' — size never overrides criticality. Typical: migrations, authn/authz, tenant isolation, a deterministic numeric core, CI and guard semantics. The declaration file itself needs no entry: its criticality is computed from which keys changed (ADR 0038 — metadata keys docs/handoff/artifacts and comments never force it; every other key always does).
review.//derived: Byte-identical placements of a canonical source — generated or vendored copies a deterministic gate holds identical (ADR 0037). A changed copy whose CURRENT bytes equal its mapped source's stops counting toward the size measure and cannot force 'critical'; a drifted copy counts fully. Path PREFIXES ending in '/' ([A-Za-z0-9._/-] only), each copy mapping directly to its canonical source — chains are not resolved. Empty disables the exemption.

retro.//: Slice retro gate (ADR 0017). Regexes, like 'review' — they select and report, so free strings are safe. An EMPTY list DISABLES the checks it drives; the disablement is reported by `harness_retro.py --coverage` rather than passing quietly.
retro.//source_scope: Product source that must be owned by a spec's implements_in. Drives UNMAPPED, which fires on NEWLY ADDED files only — new code is owned from day one and the legacy baseline does not spam every commit.
retro.//dep_manifests: Dependency manifests. Drives DEP: changed with no new ADR in scope. List the manifest, NOT the lockfile — a lockfile bump is a version change, not a decision.
retro.//migrations: Schema migration files. Drives MIGRATION: added with no living spec touched.
retro.//ignore_file: The UNMAPPED exemption list, which doubles as the visible spec-debt register.

groups.//: One entry per file family that has its own gates. 'match' is a regex anchored at the repo root; 'cwd' is where the command runs; 'strip_prefix' is removed from file paths before they are passed. 'gates' are SELECTORS: ruff | ruff-format | pytest | pytest-nondb | eslint | prettier | tsc | vitest | cargo-clippy | cargo-test | go-vet | go-test | actionlint. A gate outside the set is dropped with the set named. A gate that is this REPO'S OWN SCRIPT (a test entry point no repo-independent selector could name) is a script-gate object: {"runner": "pwsh", "script": "tools/selftest.ps1", "files": false} — runner is a selector from the verify.runner closed set, script is a repo-relative path held to an allowlist ([A-Za-z0-9._/-] only, no '..', no leading '/' or '-'; refused otherwise), files:true appends the slice's changed files. There is deliberately no argument field: a gate that needs flags wraps them inside the script (ADR 0024). Need a shared TOOL that is missing? Add it to the plugin's closed set, where it is reviewed once and reaches every repo. Paths the scaffold itself places (scripts/harness/, .githooks/, the CI workflow, the seeds, .harness-version) are claimed BUILT-IN by the emitter and need no entry here (ADR 0044) — declare groups only for files this repo authors.
groups.name: example-python

groups.//: The Claude Code host's own project settings. Claimed because `claude plugin install --scope project` writes .claude/settings.json into the tree, and an unclaimed file fails CI (and reads as missing coverage locally). Claiming it is NOT permission to commit `enabledPlugins`: that key forces the plugin on every clone, and CI and pre-commit refuse it in both settings files regardless of its value (ADR 0010, ADR 0022).
groups.name: claude-host

verify.//runner: SELECTOR: python-uv | python | poetry | node | pwsh.
verify.//script_pattern: Regex identifying a verify script inside a spec's implements_in.
verify.//product_scope: Regex for files that SHOULD have a spec owner. Matches with no owner are reported as unmapped. Empty disables the check.
verify.//ui_prefix: Path prefix whose changes the registered scripts do not cover. Empty disables the note.
